title: Starter sprint blueprint — Lyra Retail POC
content:
Purpose
This doc is the starter-sprint blueprint for the Lyra Retail POC (focus: checkout-assist & product recommendations). It’s a working plan for the first 14 days to validate technical feasibility, observed latency/cost tradeoffs, and initial quality signals. Use this during the kickoff and keep as the canonical short plan until the formal POC runbook is produced.

Scope (what we will prove in Sprint 0 -> Sprint 1)
- End-to-end hosted inference path: sample storefront -> request normalization -> Redwood hosted API -> post-processing -> UI mock.
- Latency and cost profile for 1K qps synthetic workload and realistic user traces.
- Quality sanity: recommendation relevance for top-5 recall and conversational prompt completion quality for 50 curated prompts.
- Data handling check: no PII persisted; KMS for customer config validated.

Non-goals
- Full integration with ERP or inventory sync (out of scope for starter sprint).
- Large-scale A/B experiments beyond initial canary.

Roles & contacts
- POC owner (Customer): Marina Lopez (Lyra product)
- Redwood SE lead: Avery Chen (owner of this doc)
- Solutions Eng: Priya Raman (integration lead)
- Applied ML: Diego Morales (model/quantization advisor)
- SRE/Infra: Samir Patel (capacity + observability)
- Customer success: Jordan Mills (customer enablement)

Kickoff agenda (60 minutes)
- 00–05m: Intros + success definition alignment
- 05–15m: Business scenario & demo expectations (Lyra)
- 15–30m: Technical architecture walkthrough (Redwood) — routing, model variant plan, fallback policies
- 30–40m: Data & security checklist (what Lyra can share)
- 40–50m: Sprint timeline + milestones
- 50–60m: Risks, open questions, immediate next steps

Success criteria (measurable) — all must be met for POC acceptance
1) Latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency <= 300ms on hosted endpoint for 1k requests/min baseline test (single-region).
2) Cost target: steady-state inference cost < $0.80 per 1k generated tokens under proposed quantized model profile (baseline estimate; +/- 20%).
3) Quality baseline: top-5 recommendation recall >= 0.65 on Lyra sample testset (50 labeled sessions) and conversational completion BLEU-like proxy score >= 0.6 on curated prompts.
4) Reliability: no more than 1% error rate (5xx or 4xx due to inference failures) during a 2-hour soak test at target load.
5) Data compliance: proof of KMS integration + audit log sample showing request id mapping without PII.
6) Operator readiness: SRE runbook (incident steps, rollback policy, cost throttle knobs) reviewed and accepted by Samir.

Sprint plan (14-day starter sprint)
Day 0–2: setup & minimal demo
- Provision test API key & sandbox model variant.
- Ingest 50-session sample traces from Lyra (anonymized).
- Quick smoke demo: single-turn recommendation generation.
Deliverable: interactive demo + run commands.

Day 3–7: load & performance profiling
- Run synthetic traffic using customer's session traces at incremental rates (10rps -> 200rps -> 1k/min).
- Capture latency percentiles, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates.
- Try two quantization configs (int8 and fp16) and 1–2 model sizes (base / small-latency).
Deliverable: performance matrix and tuning notes.

Day 8–11: quality eval & fallback wiring
- Run quality tests on 50 labeled prompts; compare model variants.
- Wire automatic fallback: if p95 latency > 400ms or error rate > 1.5%, route to cheaper/safer variant.
Deliverable: evaluation summary + fallback policy commit.

Day 12–14: soak & acceptance
- 2-hour soak at target traffic, monitoring dashboards live, smoke customers flows tested.
- Acceptance review session with Lyra PM.
Deliverable: acceptance checklist + signoff notes.

Experiment matrix (high level)
- Axis A: Model family (open-llm-7b, open-llm-3b-compact)
- Axis B: Quantization (fp16, int8)
- Axis C: Routing policy (latency-first, cost-first, region-fallback)
- Axis D: Cache (prefix-only, full-kv)
Run the top 6 combinations with prioritized budget: first 3 combinations = primary evaluation.

Observability & dashboards
- Token-level cost by request route (console drop-in recommended)
- Per-route p50/p95/p99 latency timeline for entire sprint window
- Error taxonomy (parse vs model vs infra) with sample request ids for triage
- Quality regression snapshot: side-by-side outputs for 50 golden prompts per variant

Data collection checklist for Lyra (what we need from customer)
- 50 anonymized session traces (JSON) with timestamps and user actions
- Example storefront snapshot (product catalog sample, images not required)
- A contact with SSO/KMS admin rights for quick KMS testing
- Network allowlist IPs or guidance for IP-restricted environments

Runbook & emergency rollback (short form)
- Step 0: Identify issue and tag example request ids in dashboard
- Step 1: If model latency > threshold, trigger policy to route to fallback variant (auto)
- Step 2: Notify customer and SRE channel (#sre-lyra) with incident template
- Step 3: If repeated inference errors, disable model route and switch to a static-recommendation stub until resolved
- Postmortem: <72 hours after incident with action items

Open questions / known risks (to surface in kickoff)
- Customer can only provide coarse-grained product catalog snapshots, not full IDs — will it affect recall evaluation? (ACTION: Priya to test mapping heuristics).
- Expected production qps unclear; plan uses 1k/min baseline but need high-water estimate. (ACTION: Marina to confirm).
- KMS IAM policy changes could add 48–72h delay; pre-approve service account where possible.

Acceptance checklist (to be signed by Lyra PM)
- [ ] Demo reproduces recommendation flow end-to-end
- [ ] p95 latency < 300ms measured on annotated run
- [ ] Quality baseline met (top-5 recall + conversational proxy)
- [ ] SRE runbook accepted and accessible in Confluence
- [ ] Security checklist: KMS + minimal logs without PII

Notes to self (choppy)
- bring quick synthetic script to kickoff so they can run locally
- prioritize int8 baseline if GPU mem looks tight
- remember to show cost dashboard that maps tokens -> dollars (customer loves $$ numbers)

Next steps (immediately after kickoff)
1) Priya to create SE-5234 sub-tasks and assign (integration, data-cleaning, test harness)
2) Samir to drop sample dashboard and invite Lyra SREs to view-only console
3) Avery to schedule daily 15m stand for first week and end-of-sprint review; calendar invite to be sent

Appendix: quick checklist for demo run locally
- install redwood-cli: pip install redwood-inference-cli (or use docker image)
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=se_..._sandbox
- run: redwood-cli run-demo --variant small-latency --input sample-session.json
- artifacts: save request ids in ./run-artifacts/ for postmortem linking

End of starter blueprint — keep iterative and jot changes in this doc.
